skeptical-audit.why: the change extends this skill's own evidence discipline to the mistakes made before and around a claim (ownership assumptions, cherry-picked headlines, un-next-stepped downgrades, done-on-inferred, unmeasured comparisons).
skeptical-audit.what: added section 7 to the evidence contract and five claim-lint rules (ownership, downgrade-names-next-step, headline-predeclared, done-needs-observed-majority, comparison-needs-measurement), and extended the one-rule line so a downgrade names its next step.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

verifiable-quality-gates.why: each of the five new claim-lint rules is a check whose detection must be proven, so each ships a committed test that flags the bad case and passes the good one (and fails if the rule is a no-op).
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added discriminating test pairs for the ownership, downgrade, headline, done-inferred, and comparison rules to the claim-lint test; a no-op claim-lint flips the must-flag cases.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the five acceptance scenarios for this issue are added to the executable harness and driven by step definitions that run the real claim-lint, so they execute rather than only parse.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added the five skeptical-audit-addition scenarios to features/evidence/claims-match-evidence.feature with step defs in skeptical-additions.steps.mjs (reusing the shared 'the mark is refused' step), and regenerated the datastore + coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

architectural-decision-records.why: adding five evidence-discipline rules and choosing how to enforce each is a significant decision with real alternatives, so it ships an ADR in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0093 recording the five additions, the documentation-plus-smoke-alarm choice, and the ownership rule's split (smoke alarm now, edit-time block in #175), with considered options and named limits.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

pattern-selector.why: the ownership rule had two shapes (a claim-lint smoke alarm vs blocking the edit at the #175 hook) and the decision names the structure chosen on purpose and where the real enforcement lives.
pattern-selector.what: chose the smoke-alarm-now plus edit-time-block-later split for ownership, and document-level tallying for done-needs-observed-majority, recorded in ADR-0093's considered options with the forces and the discriminating tests as the guarantee.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the new rules are tested at the layer that owns the risk - integration tests that spawn the real claim-lint against fixtures, matching the test type to the risk.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added bad/good fixture pairs that run the real claim-lint for each of the five rules, plus the no-false-positive good cases.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

judge-arch.why: adding five heuristic rules to a shared checker risks false positives, so it must pass a fresh-context review against the four questions before it is done.
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context subagent review of the full diff (false-positive hunt on each rule, regressions, the shared-step reuse, docs-vs-code, discrimination), resolved its findings, and recorded the review in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: offline evidence-discipline tooling over repo-local trusted report drafts; no untrusted input, auth, secret, network, or user-facing surface; the script makes no outbound web calls (arch gate enforces).

arch-encode.why: the audit findings are encoded as claim-lint rules plus the evidence contract section 7, each pinned by its own discriminating test, not as a new nearest-scoped AGENTS.md/decisions.md negative-example rule.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, retention, migration, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no running system, service boundary, data model, or scaling surface; a report linter plus skill docs.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or rollback of a running system.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing UI; no .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css surface in the change.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no interactive user-facing surface; the skill docs follow house style but there is no UI or flow.
